To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitization rate to ragweed and olive pollen increased significantly in Germany between 2001 and 2017 and that the sensitization prevalence is associated with the pollen concentration and spreading capacity of the respective pollen species.

the pollen season length of the allergenic pollen of ragweed (Ambrosia artemisiifolia) and olive (Olea europaea) is increasing in the federal states of North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW) and Bavaria, Germany, and that the pollen season is shifting to earlier dates.
the sensitization to ragweed and olive pollen has been increasing in Germany in the last 20 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential risk of climate change associated allergenic pollen spreading capacity for two important allergenic plants, the common ragweed and olive.
the question of how climate change affects the spreading of allergenic pollen, which in turn affects the sensitization of patients with pollen allergy and thus their health.
the question of how the sensitization to allergenic pollen changes with increasing pollen spreading capacity due to climate change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for a significant increase of pollen sensitization in Germany in the last decades, but the number of patients with pollen sensitization has not decreased, either.
ragweed and olive pollen are a potential health hazard in Germany, especially in the federal states of Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Hessen and North Rhine-Westphalia.
the pollen season of olive and ragweed will become longer, with a shift in the start of the season, in both Germany and the Mediterranean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not yet ready to make a statement about the health risk of allergen pollen in the future.
ragweed and olive are two important pollen sources in Germany, and that ragweed pollen is a major source of allergen in the air.
the climate change-associated increase of ragweed pollen and olive sensitization is a potential health risk in Germany.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ragweed is a serious allergen that is becoming more common.
the pollen season for ragweed and olive is increasing in Germany.
the risk of allergic reactions to pollen is increasing.
